answer: Jury-consensus slashing prices grading. Each answer draws a 7-juror panel by sortition, and every juror bonds coin before scoring. Payout flows only to grades matching the settled 4-of-7 verdict; seeded honeypot answers catch jurors rubber-stamping junk, burning that bond plus a 48-epoch seat ban. So a Sybil cannot fly a falcon-swift vote-ring over the glacier: flipping one verdict means capturing 4 seats at once, yet sortition scatters its clones, forcing a separate bonded, honest-track-record identity per seat, not a free copy. Collusion slashes in a tightening spiral faster than it earns.
